title: SDK Developer Garden: Checklist + Lab Journal
content:
Purpose:
This is a working journal for a tiny, repeatable instructor-led lab we call the "Developer Garden" — a 60–90 minute hands-on fast-path for engineers unfamiliar with Redwood SDKs. The goal is to give a reproducible, low-friction flow that ends with a small, instrumented demo and a checklist teams can use to run the lab themselves.

Audience:
- New engineers evaluating Redwood SDKs
- Solutions engineers running in-product workshops
- Internal docs authors who will copy/paste task lists into official quickstarts

Outcome (what success looks like):
- Participant runs local sample app and gets a streamed chat response within ~10 minutes.
- Basic telemetry appears in our sandbox console: request id, latency, token count.
- Participant can toggle a fallback model and observe graceful degradation.
- A 1-paragraph writeup for post-lab follow-up is produced by each participant.

High-level flow (60–90m)
- 0–10m: Welcome + goals + prereqs (Git, node/python, API key).
- 10–25m: Quick install + `hello-world` sample (JS + Py snippets below).
- 25–50m: Add streaming + error handling + simple retry policy.
- 50–70m: Add telemetry hook and lightweight assertions (smoke test).
- 70–90m: Canary toggle exercise: swap model variant, run small load, note latency/cost change.

Prereqs checklist (quick to skim)
- [ ] Redwood sandbox account + temporary API key (link in invite)
- [ ] Node 18+ or Python 3.10+ installed
- [ ] Git client and basic familiarity
- [ ] Docker optional for hermetic mode (we include a docker-compose for the sample app)
- [ ] Slack channel pre-created for the workshop (eg #devgarden-<date>)

Quick install (copy/paste)
- JS (npm):
  - npm init -y
  - npm install @redwood/sdk@latest
  - export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk-test-..."
  - node hello-chat.js

- Python (pip):
  - python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
  - pip install redwood-sdk
  - export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk-test-..."
  - python hello_chat.py

Minimal hello-chat example (JS) — paste into hello-chat.js:
- const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk')
- async function main(){
-   const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
-   const res = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-small-v1', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Write a 3-line haiku about debugging.' }] })
-   console.log(res.choices[0].message.content)
- }
- main()

Minimal hello_chat.py (Python):
- from redwood import RedwoodClient
- client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
- resp = client.chat.create(model='redwood-small-v1', messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Explain prefix caching in one paragraph."}])
- print(resp.choices[0].message['content'])

Instructor tips and fallbacks (notes-to-self):
- If streaming stalls: check network + proxy. Ask participant to run `curl -v https://api.redwood.example/health` to confirm baseline.
- If API key not accepted: confirm no stray whitespace, try `echo -n $REDWOOD_API_KEY | wc -c` to ensure length.
- For slow token counts: show how to enable soft-prefix caching by toggling sample config in .redwoodrc.
- If Docker image fails on M1 Macs: use the lightweight node-only variant (we keep a note in the repo).

Telemetry + smoke tests (fast):
- Hook: After each request, post a small event to the sandbox console endpoint: "/client/ingest/telemetry" with fields: request_id, model, duration_ms, token_count
- Smoke assertions (runnable shell commands):
  - curl -sS "https://sandbox.console/api/requests/latest?api_key=$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | jq '.requests[0] | {id: .id, duration: .duration_ms, tokens: .token_count}'
  - Exit nonzero if duration > 1200ms (teaching point: latency SLO discussion)

Canary toggle exercise (short):
- Show controlled model switch in code: `model: process.env.FALLBACK_MODEL ?? 'redwood-small-v1'`
- Run small batch (10 sequential requests) and capture mean latency + cost tokens
- Ask participants to flip to a quantized variant (eg redwood-small-qat) and observe tradeoffs in latency vs output quirks. Capture notes in the post-lab writeup.

Common gotchas observed in prior runs (journal entries):
- People paste full API key with quotes — remove them
- Windows PowerShell users often mis-set env vars — provide PS-specific commands
- Participants expect function calling by default; call out that explicit schema is required and provide a tiny example schema file
- Network proxies in corporate environments may rewrite chunked transfer; have a non-chunked fallback sample ready

Post-lab deliverables (participant actions)
- Short writeup (3–5 sentences): what they built, a perf observation, one unresolved question.
- Optional PR: copy sample into their repo and open PR with a single `README: add redwood quickstart` commit; tag `#devgarden` so SEs can pick up for follow-up.

Acceptance criteria for making this a published quickstart page:
- Repro steps verified on Linux, macOS (Intel + Apple Silicon), and Windows PowerShell (basic)
- Minimal app runs without Docker and with Docker
- Telemetry examples return data to sandbox console within 2 minutes of request
- Workshop script has a clear 60-minute version and an extended 90-minute version

Open questions / experiments to trial:
- Should we make the lab default to a conversation cohort (multi-turn) or single-response? (proposal: start single-response for speed, then optional extension to multi-turn)
- Do we include a one-click GitHub Codespace template? (high leverage, ops cost to maintain)
- Automate API-key provisioning for sandbox via short-lived tokens in a workshop invite? (Security reviews needed)

TODOs (action items)
- [ ] Clean up the example repo so the node and py samples are one-directory copy/paste ready (Marcus)
- [ ] Add PS examples and common env var pitfalls to the README (Priya)
- [ ] Draft simple instructor script + slide deck (Tomás)
- [ ] Add a tiny non-chunked HTTP sample for corporate proxies (Elena)

Quick reference: useful commands and links
- Check environment: `node -v && python -V && git --version`
- Start example app: `npm run dev` or `python -m sampleapp`
- Sandbox console: https://sandbox.console.redwood.example/ (use workshop API key)
- Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devgarden-samples

Final note (meta):
This doc is deliberately rough — the Developer Garden should be a low-friction, frequently iterated artifact. Keep journal entries short and move changes into the canonical quickstart when the flow stabilizes after three workshops.

End of journal entry.
